intro.title: about me, briefly
paragraphs: I'm someone who thinks too much, makes things too often, and finishes maybe a third of them. I like understanding how the universe works and also how to draw a decent cartoon face. These two interests coexist peacefully.

I grew up mostly online and partly outside, in that order. I care about ideas more than small talk, prefer a good question to a good answer, and I am, statistically, always in the middle of at least three books.

timeline.title: life in a nutshell
timeline.intro: Every event below can be clicked open, if you're curious. Most of them are true. All of them are exaggerated slightly.

thinking.title: how I think
paragraphs: My brain runs on tangents. Ask me one question and you will, within four minutes, end up somewhere about octopus cognition or the Roman aqueduct system. I think in pictures more than words, in systems more than facts, and I have an unreasonable need to understand why before I accept what.
I do my best thinking late at night, in the shower, or on long walks — never at a desk, which is inconvenient, because that's where all my notebooks are.
thinking.note: "half of my best ideas arrive at 1am and are gone by breakfast."

facts.eyebrow: a random fact generator, because why not
facts.title: random facts about me
items: I have st rong, unwavering opinions about fonts.
I have never finished a to-do list. Not once.
I talk to myself when debugging. It usually works.
I own more notebooks than I have finished ideas.
I can explain black holes but I still can't parallel park.
My browser has approximately 47 tabs open right now.
I once stayed up all night for a meteor shower and saw one meteor.
